title: Anticipatory load trimmer with gossip-based regional backpressure (hotpatch)
author: Priya Nambiar
release_notes: Hotpatch: add anticipatory load trimming with cross-proxy gossip to reduce cascading retries and stabilize SLOs during short regional surges.
body:
Motivation: During the 2026-02-22 regional surge incident we observed cascading retry amplification and persistent p99 SLO breaches in the eu-west cluster. Existing circuit breakers reacted too late and per-node shedders were oscillating, causing tenant starvation and repeated requeues. This PR introduces an anticipatory, quota-aware load trimming policy that forecasts short-term queue pressure and issues soft drops for low-priority requests before queues saturate. It also adds a lightweight gossip protocol between edge proxies to share short-term queue forecasts so neighboring nodes avoid synchronized shedding spikes.

Design summary: single continuous change set implementing a new policy object (AnticipatoryLoadTrimmer) in the runtime proxy. Key characteristics: forecast window = 500-1500ms, priority-weighted trimming using tenant SLA weight, hysteresis to prevent flip-flops, and cross-proxy smoothing via a small gossip payload (3 keys: queue_estimate, last_updated, node_weight). The algorithm prefers local in-memory KV cache hits and only trims requests whose configured importance <= LOW. On loss of gossip messages the policy falls back to the existing local token-bucket shedder and sticky-circuit behavior.

Feature gating and rollout: behind feature-flag runtime.enable_anticipatory_trimmer (default false). Small canary enabled for region eu-west-1 and for Dedicated customers only. Added remote-config flag to allow per-tenant opt-out. The rollout plan: experimental in perf-canary -> 24h smoke -> broad canary -> full enable if SLO delta < 0.5%.

Implementation details: - New class: proxy/shedder/anticipatory_trimmer.go - Gossip component: proxy/gossip/queue_forecast.go (UDP-based, bounded small payload, integrated into existing heartbeat loop) - Config: added to runtime/config.yaml and runtime/feature_flags.go - Metrics: anticipatory_trim{result=(dropped|soft_pass|bypassed)}, queue_forecast_estimate_ms, gossip_messages_received_total - Tests: unit tests for forecast window and hysteresis, integration test in perf-canary harness that replays production traces with injected surge.

Performance and safety: Load tests against perf-canary traces show p99 tail latency reduced by ~18% under surge scenarios vs baseline; global request drop rate increased by 0.9% skewed to LOW-priority requests only. No measurable change to average token cost. The gossip payload adds ~120B per heartbeat per proxy (negligible). Hysteresis and backoff timers avoid re-open storms.

Files changed (high level): - proxy/shedder/anticipatory_trimmer.go (new) - proxy/gossip/queue_forecast.go (new) - runtime/config.yaml (tweak) - runtime/feature_flags.go (tweak) - tests/interval_surge_simulation_test.go (new) - perf-canary/job-configs/anticipatory-trimmer.json (new) - docs/operations/anticipatory-trimmer.md (new)

Commits: ["a1b3c4c add anticipatory trimmer skeleton and interfaces", "b2d4f8e implement gossip forecast sharing + unit tests", "c3e7a1f hotpatch: tune hysteresis/backoff timers and update docs"]

Review conversation: Reviewer Hannah Lee: "Nice approach, reduces coupling to the global SLO enforcer. Please add an e2e that verifies no tenant gets starved when gossip is partitioned." Author reply (Priya): "Added perf-canary trace that simulates partial partition in tests/interval_surge_simulation_test.go and verified per-tenant fairness metrics remain within bounds. See second commit." Reviewer Diego Morales: "One concern: UDP gossip may be dropped in noisy networks. Can we detect persistent misses and fall back faster?" Author: "Yes — added detection logic: if gossip_messages_received < 3 over 10s we halve the forecast window and rely on local token-bucket for trimming. Documented fallback in operations doc." Reviewer Samir Kothari: "CI flaked on integration test initially (timeout). Reran and passed. Approving now."

CI: Initial CI run failed on a flaky integration test (timing) - workaround: increased test timeout and added deterministic clock in tests. Reran CI: all checks passed. Jobs: go-build (pass), unit-tests (pass), integration-perf (pass), lint (pass), docs-check (pass).

Rollout notes and mitigation: - Feature flag controls canary scope; recommend 6h small canary with close monitoring of anticipatory_trim.dropped.by_priority and p99 latency. - If observed unfairness: set runtime.enable_anticipatory_trimmer=false and reboot proxies in canary set. - On partial-deploy issues the sticky-circuit (existing) provides a safe fallback path.

Related: Linear ENG-2039 (investigation), ENG-2042 (implementation); SUP-4182 recorded customer-facing impact.

This PR is a hotpatch introduced to reduce incident blast radius during short surges and to stabilize SLOs while longer-term capacity and routing adjustments are coordinated.
comments: Hannah Lee: please add e2e for gossip partitioning; otherwise looks good.
Priya Nambiar: added partitioned perf-canary test and tuned hysteresis timers (second commit).
Samir Kothari: CI flake fixed, approving.
Release lead (Marta Ivanov): merging as squash hotpatch per incident playbook.
